behaviors.behavior: qPsMultiline() never emits a raw \r/\n onto the wire for a multi-line PowerShell arg, and passes through unchanged (byte-identical to qPs()) when the input has no \r/\n
behaviors.evidence: shell-quote.test.ts — "no newline in the input", "a newline in the input → no raw newline or carriage return", "a lone \r (no \n) also takes the base64-safe path"

behaviors.behavior: The Base64 sub-expression qPsMultiline() emits decodes back to the exact original multi-paragraph, single-quote-containing, multi-byte-UTF-8 prompt text before the enclosing command ever runs
behaviors.evidence: shell-quote.test.ts — "decodes back to the exact original text", "a single quote AND a newline", "multi-byte UTF-8 content (umlaut, emoji) round-trips exactly"; launcher-codex.test.ts — "powershell form decodes back to the exact original multi-line prompt"

behaviors.behavior: Only the PowerShell render form of a fresh Codex launch is changed — cmd/posix forms and the resume path (threadId only, no prompt text) remain byte-identical to before the fix
behaviors.evidence: launcher-codex.test.ts — "powershell form contains no raw newline even for a multi-paragraph prompt", "cmd and posix forms are untouched -- the fix is scoped to PowerShell only"

surface_verification.justification: The bug's causal layer is the real PowerShell/PSReadLine process, not the browser/xterm layer -- a Playwright browser E2E would exercise the xterm.js DOM/WS path, not the actual defect mechanism (PSReadLine's own multi-line edit-buffer corruption on pty keystroke injection). This was verified directly against a real pwsh.exe via node-pty (both the production ChunkedPtyWriter path and an atomic single pty.write() path): the pre-fix command reproduced the exact reported error, the post-fix command launched `codex` cleanly and reached its TUI. Launching a genuine Codex CLI agent process from an automated E2E test would be disproportionate scope/risk for a shell-quoting fix and would contradict this repo's own established precedent (runtime-toggle-codex.spec.ts AC8 explicitly avoids depending on the Codex CLI being present on every machine including CI, for portability).
